g1|variants|resource-related billing.summary: Resource-related billing enables companies to bill customers for incurred costs such as labor, materials, and expenses captured on dynamic items like service orders, projects, or SD documents. Variants differ based on the underlying object type, pricing source, and billing document creation path.

variants.when_used: Billing customers for labor, spare parts, and expenses recorded on customer service orders.
variants.key_config: DIP profile configuration for service orders, maintenance category settings, and pricing source determination via DIP.

variants.key_config: Intercompany billing type settings, customer-vendor linking for company codes, and pricing procedure setup for intercompany.

g1|core|resource-related billing|project.title: Project-Based Resource-Related Billing
g1|core|resource-related billing|project.story: Imagine a big company sends workers and materials to build a bridge, and at the end of the month, the computer magically turns all those timesheets and spare parts into a customer bill. In SAP S/4HANA, project-based resource-related billing reads actual costs recorded on a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) element or network, uses the Dynamic Item Processor to dynamically aggregate these items via a DIP profile, and generates a debit memo request for invoicing.
g1|core|resource-related billing|project.why_business_needs_it: Professional services and engineering companies cannot use fixed-price billing when project tasks vary constantly; they must bill clients accurately for every hour worked and material consumed. This automated process bridges project accounting and Order-to-Cash, ensuring all incurred costs are captured and billed to maximize revenue leakage prevention.

modules.hands_off_to: SD (Sales and Distribution) via DP91 for resource-related billing creation.

g1|core|resource-related billing|service.title: Service Order Resource-Related Billing
g1|core|resource-related billing|service.story: Just like a mechanic fixes your car and charges you for the exact hours worked and parts used, this process bills customers for actual service resources consumed. In SAP S/4HANA, a Plant Maintenance (PM) or Customer Service (CS) service order collects actual labor, material, and expense costs, which the Dynamic Item Processor (DIP) then turns into a billing request and invoice. This ensures that every hour of technician work and every spare part is accurately billed to the customer based on agreed contract rates.
g1|core|resource-related billing|service.why_business_needs_it: Service businesses cannot always charge a flat fee because repair and maintenance work varies significantly in duration and materials. Resource-related billing bridges Plant Maintenance operations and Order-to-Cash (OTC) finance by converting operational confirmations into precise customer invoices, protecting profit margins.

g1|core|resource-related billing|sales d.title: Sales Document Resource-Related Billing
g1|core|resource-related billing|sales d.story: Just like a mechanic writes down every extra hour and part used to fix a broken bicycle and charges you for them, this process captures everyday costs from sales orders and turns them into custom customer bills. More technically, the Dynamic Item Processor evaluates actual expenditures logged against a sales order item using profile SD02 to generate a debit memo request before final invoicing.
g1|core|resource-related billing|sales d.why_business_needs_it: Companies offering specialized consulting, ad-hoc services, or variable material consumption cannot use fixed-price billing and must bill customers dynamically based on actual resource consumption. This ensures accurate revenue recognition and profitability tracking for non-standard sales order engagements.

g1|core|resource-related billing|interco.title: Intercompany Resource-Related Billing
g1|core|resource-related billing|interco.story: Imagine your company rents out expert consultants or equipment to another branch of the same global enterprise, and the system automatically creates an invoice between the two sister companies based on the exact hours or materials used. Technically, Intercompany Resource-Related Billing captures cross-company expenses recorded on a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) element or internal order in the ordering company, processes them using the Dynamic Item Processor (DIP), generates a debit memo request or intercompany billing request, and creates an SD billing document (IV) from the delivering company to the ordering company.
g1|core|resource-related billing|interco.why_business_needs_it: Multinational enterprises require legal entities to charge each other accurately for cross-company resource utilization to maintain proper transfer pricing and compliance. Without this automated intercompany billing flow, manual cross-company recharges fail audits and delay group-level financial consolidation.

modules.role: Tracks the project structure, WBS elements, and actual cost postings from cross-company resource usage.
modules.hands_off_to: SD to trigger resource-related billing via the DIP.

modules.role: Processes the intercompany billing request, manages pricing, and generates the intercompany billing document (IV).
modules.hands_off_to: FI to post intercompany accounts receivable and accounts payable postings.

modules.role: Receives the intercompany billing document data to post intercompany vendor invoices and customer receivables.

g1|panel|resource-related billing.otc_impact: Resource-related billing sits at the intersection of service execution, project management, and Order-to-Cash, transforming actual incurred costs and labor hours into customer invoices. It impacts OTC by converting dynamic consumption data into billing requests through transaction DP90, driving downstream SD billing documents, revenue recognition, and cash collection. If misconfigured, billing delays erode working capital, unbilled items accumulate in WIP, and customer disputes rise due to lack of traceable service evidence.

panel_qa.question: How do we choose between Project-Based, Service Order, and Sales Document Resource-Related Billing for our professional services and field maintenance operations?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Resource-related billing must align with the operational execution vehicle to ensure accurate cost capture and transparent customer invoicing. Project-Based billing using SAP S/4HANA Project Systems (PS) or Enterprise Portfolio and Project Management (EPPM) is selected for complex engagements requiring WBS elements and network activities. Service Order billing is utilized for field service and repair scenarios executed via Customer Service (CS) or Service Management (SM) orders, capturing labor, spare parts, and expenses directly. Sales Document billing is deployed for straightforward quotation-to-cash scenarios linked directly to SD order items without underlying projects or service orders. The key configuration relies on dynamic item processor (DIP) profiles mapped via transaction OIN0 to define source tables, such as ACDOCA or JCDS, and materiality filters. This approach ensures operational traceability while maintaining standard OTC hand-offs to debit memo requests and billing documents.
panel_qa.trap: We use Project-Based billing for everything because it is the most robust project accounting tool available in SAP S/4HANA.

panel_qa.question: What is the financial and operational impact of Intercompany Resource-Related Billing on our consolidated revenue and transfer pricing compliance?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Intercompany resource-related billing automates the rebilling of cross-affiliate labor and expenses incurred when resources from one company code deliver services to a customer billed by another. This process ensures statutory compliance, accurate transfer pricing, and correct profit center accounting across legal entities within the SAP enterprise structure. Technically, the delivering company posts time or expenses to an internal order or project, which triggers an intercompany billing request using pricing procedure RVAA01 with specific intercompany condition types. The receiving company then includes these costs in the external customer billing document generated via transaction DP90. Leadership benefits from auditable cross-company margins, reduced manual journal entries, and accelerated intercompany reconciliation, protecting group EBITDA and audit readiness. Next, we are optimizing automated batch jobs in transaction DP90 to run nightly for all intercompany projects.
panel_qa.trap: Intercompany resource billing is just an internal accounting journal entry, so we do not need to set up full SD intercompany billing documents.

panel_qa.question: How do we prevent revenue leakage and unbilled items piling up in WIP when engineers delay entering their timesheets or service confirmations?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Timely resource-related billing depends entirely on front-line operational discipline in recording labor and material consumption against projects or service orders. We mitigate revenue leakage by enforcing strict closure dates, implementing SAP Fiori apps for mobile time entry, and establishing automated alerts for unbilled items sitting in Work in Process (WIP). Technically, unbilled quantities are identified by comparing actual postings in table ACDOCA against already billed quantities recorded in table VBSEDI via dynamic item processor profiles in transaction OIN0. From an OTC perspective, we monitor DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) and unbilled revenue KPIs through dedicated SAP Analytics Cloud dashboards to spot bottlenecks before month-end close. Next, we are introducing automated workflow notifications for project managers to review unbilled resource requests weekly.
panel_qa.trap: Engineers will naturally enter their time on Fridays, so we do not need automated reminders or system blocks for unsubmitted timesheets.

steps.step: Execute Dynamic Item Processor to generate billing request from WBS element.
steps.data: Profile IC01, WBS Element W-1000-01, Sales Organization 1010
steps.expected: System generates Intercompany Debit Memo Request and displays success message with document number.

steps.step: Review and remove billing block on the generated Debit Memo Request.
steps.data: Debit Memo Request order number from DP91, remove billing block field
steps.expected: Sales document status changes to unblocked for billing.

steps.step: Create Intercompany Billing Document from the debit memo request.
steps.data: Billing Type IV, Sales Document from previous step
steps.expected: Billing document IV is created and accounting document is posted successfully.

test_cases.expected_result: Intercompany billing document created successfully with complete financial and SD postings.
test_cases.documents_created: Debit Memo Request 70000001, Billing Document 90000001, Accounting Document 190000001

test_cases.title: Missing Dynamic Item Processor Source Data
test_cases.preconditions: WBS element has no unbilled actual costs or hours posted.

steps.step: Execute Dynamic Item Processor for WBS element without costs.
steps.data: Profile IC01, WBS Element W-1000-99, Sales Organization 1010
steps.expected: System displays error message indicating no source items found for billing.

test_cases.expected_result: System prevents creation of billing request and issues message VP015 (No dynamic items found).

test_cases.title: Unassigned Delivering Plant in Intercompany Customizing
test_cases.preconditions: Plant and sales organization combination lacks assignment in table TVRO via transaction OVP4.

steps.step: Attempt to create intercompany billing document for unassigned plant combination.
steps.data: Billing Type IV, Sales Document referencing unassigned plant
steps.expected: System triggers pricing or partner determination error during billing creation.

test_cases.expected_result: System blocks billing creation with error message VF045 (Intercompany billing configuration missing for plant).
